blocks.passage:
Every international payment is a trade-off between three things: speed, cost and risk. A SWIFT wire is reliable and global but takes one to three days and costs money. A correspondent banking chain is cheap but slower and less transparent. A fintech rail can be faster and cheaper, but may be less widely accepted.

The right choice depends on what you need. For a small, urgent payment to a known supplier, speed matters most. For a large, high-value payment, certainty matters most. For routine payments to many suppliers, cost and ease of reconciliation usually win.

The best treasury teams do not use one method for everything. They match the method to the situation, and they review the choice as new options appear.

audio.text:
You've got a recurring payment to an Asian supplier and you're asking whether to stick with a SWIFT wire or move to a fintech rail. Let me weigh it up with you.

Start with the situation. This isn't a one-off; it's the same supplier, same amount, every month. That changes things — for a recurring, predictable payment, cost and ease of reconciliation matter more than raw speed.

The SWIFT wire you use now is rock-solid and everyone accepts it, but it's the most expensive option, and honestly, for a routine payment, you're paying a premium for a certainty you don't strictly need with a supplier you trust.

The fintech rail is cheaper and faster, and it reconciles automatically, which would save your team time every month. The only real question is acceptance — does this supplier's bank take it cleanly? If yes, it's the better fit here.

So my advice: test the fintech rail on one month's payment. If it lands cleanly and reconciles, switch. If there's any friction, stay on SWIFT. Low risk to try, real savings if it works.

items.q: "A **SWIFT wire** is a…"
options: bank-to-bank international transfer via the SWIFT network
items.why: SWIFT wire = transferência internacional pela rede SWIFT.

items.q: **Reconciliation** in payments means…
items.why: Reconciliation = conciliação (bater pagamentos com faturas).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "For a big payment, **___** matters most."
items.why: Certainty = certeza.

items.q: "The method is **reliable**." Reliable means…
items.why: Reliable = confiável.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "A **payment ___** is the route a payment travels."
items.why: Payment rail = trilho/via de pagamento.

items.q: "Let me **weigh it up** with you." To weigh up means to…
items.why: Weigh up = ponderar.

items.q: "For now, let's **stick with** SWIFT." To stick with means to…
items.why: Stick with = manter, continuar com.

items.q: "You're **paying a premium** for certainty." To pay a premium means to…
items.why: Pay a premium = pagar mais caro.

items.q: "Let's **try it out** on one payment." To try something out means to…
items.why: Try out = experimentar, testar.

items.q: "If there's any **friction**, stay on SWIFT." Friction here means…
options: difficulty or resistance in the process
items.why: Friction = atrito, dificuldade no processo.
